tagline: Back roads of the old Irish Settlement, past Kerr's brick mill.
intro: The byway leaves NC 150 west of Salisbury on Sherrills Ford Road and wanders the farm roads of western Rowan County around Mount Ulla and Mill Bridge, by Kerr Mill Road, Millbridge Road and Corriher Springs Road. It is open country of fields, streams and working farms, with about 50 people to the square mile.

The first recorded settlement here was the Irish Settlement of 1747 to 1749, and Thyatira Presbyterian Church was established before 1750. Nobody is sure where the name Mount Ulla came from. It may be an Irish village, a man in the Book of Chronicles, or Ulaid, the old Irish kingdom that gave Ulster its name.

moments.title: Mill Bridge
moments.text: The little farm community centered on Thyatira Presbyterian Church, and for the 29 years it had a post office of its own, every postmaster was a woman.

moments.title: Kerr Mill
moments.text: A two-story brick grist mill of 1823 that ground for one owner after another until the 1940s, offered to the county in 1973 and kept now as a museum in Sloan Park.

moments.title: Mount Ulla
moments.text: In 2019 residents hung a 500-square-foot community barn quilt on a store wall at Bear Poplar, the largest in the country until nearby Cleveland put up a bigger one in 2021.
